query_list_permutation.assumptions: Mathematically deterministic, independent pair evaluator f(X,q); no claim about finite-precision runtime batching or packed query interaction.
query_list_permutation.implication: List-order equivariance holds for every such evaluator, including entity-aware uniform and classical scorers. It cannot distinguish Q-RMEA or imply semantic inverse-label equivariance.

complex_direction_scalar_example.implication: A signed complex relational score can be asymmetric while direct squared modulus of this same scalar erases its sign. Classical complex directionality is known; moving a source property through an absolute square needs a separate proof.
complex_direction_scalar_example.native_model_limit: This scalar formula is not Q-RMEA's query-marked H plus explicit R preparation, class effect, normalized token attention and signed-value decoder. It proves neither native swap symmetry nor inability or utility. It assumes no natural inverse-label law.

encoder_reuse_boundary.source: PURE publisher PDF p5 section3.3; PL-Marker publisher PDF pp3-4 sections3.1/3.3.
encoder_reuse_boundary.source_fact: PURE approximation blocks original text from attending to query markers and ties marker positions so text representations can be reused. Original pair-marked models do not enforce this same mask.
encoder_reuse_boundary.implication: Same raw tokens do not certify invariant contextual H under changed entity query. Adopting a changed mask/encoder is a changed model, with new evidence required; original scoped L4 does not transfer.
